<explanation>
1. Project type and purpose  
   - ToolHive is a multi-component Go-based system that provides a CLI, a local container runner (“proxyrunner”), an HTTP/gRPC API server, and a Kubernetes Operator to deploy and manage Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers in secure containers.  
   - It supports local (Docker) and cluster (Kubernetes) deployment, secrets management, telemetry, and pluggable registries/auth.

2. High-level components  
   a. CLI client (“thv” binary under cmd/thv)  
   b. Local runner (“proxyrunner” binary under cmd/thv-proxyrunner)  
   c. API server (pkg/api exposing HTTP/JSON endpoints)  
   d. Kubernetes Operator (cmd/thv-operator + deploy/charts/operator)  
   e. Container runtime interfaces (pkg/container/docker, pkg/container/kubernetes)  
   f. Secrets & config backends (pkg/secrets, pkg/config, pkg/state)  
   g. Registry providers (pkg/registry/provider_{local,remote})  
   h. Authn/Authz middleware (pkg/auth, pkg/authz)  
   i. Telemetry & audit (pkg/telemetry, pkg/audit)  
   j. External services: Docker/K8s API, container registries, OIDC providers (Keycloak/GitHub), telemetry backends (Prometheus/OTLP/Jaeger)

3. Relationships and data flows  
   - CLI “thv” → API server (HTTP/gRPC) for registry discovery, group management, and remote control  
   - CLI “thv” → direct container runtime calls (Docker or K8s) via pkg/container for local mode  
   - API server → registry providers to fetch available MCP tool definitions  
   - CLI/Operator → secrets manager for fetching credentials (1Password, keyring, env)  
   - CLI → proxyrunner via STDIO/SSE/streamable proxy for bidirectional tunnel to MCP server process  
   - Operator watches CRDs (MCPServer, MCPRegistry, ToolConfig) using controllers → creates Kubernetes Deployments (mcpserver + proxyrunner sidecar) via Helm chart  
   - Telemetry middleware intercepts HTTP and SSE traffic → pushes metrics/traces to OTLP or Prometheus  
   - Audit middleware logs events to audit sink

4. Architectural patterns and design principles  
   - Modular Go packages following “pkg/…” for domain separation (auth, audit, registry, container, transport, secrets, telemetry)  
   - Adapter/factory patterns for pluggable implementations (registry providers, secrets stores, transport layers)  
   - Operator pattern for Kubernetes CRD reconciliation (controller-runtime)  
   - Middleware chaining (HTTP handlers for auth, audit, telemetry)  
   - State abstraction (local file vs. Kubernetes API)  

5. Diagramming guidelines  
   - Use distinct shapes/colors for:
     • CLI & proxyrunner (client-side tools)  
     • API Server and controllers (backend)  
     • Kubernetes cluster boundary vs. Local Docker boundary  
     • External systems (registry, OIDC, telemetry, Docker daemon)  
   - Draw directional arrows:
     • Commands and control flows (CLI → API, CLI → container runtime, Operator → K8s API)  
     • Data flows (API → registry provider, container logs → telemetry, audit events → sink)  
   - Layer separation:
     1. User layer (CLI, UI)  
     2. Control layer (API server, Operator)  
     3. Execution layer (container runtime, pods, proxyrunner)  
     4. Infrastructure layer (Kubernetes API, Docker daemon, external services)  

6. Tailoring to ToolHive specifics  
   - Highlight “thv” CLI connecting to both local runtime (pkg/container/docker) and remote API  
   - Show “proxyrunner” as a sidecar or local service enabling STDIO/SSE/HTTP proxy to the MCP server process  
   - Represent the Kubernetes Operator reading CRDs and deploying two container types per MCPServer (mcpserver + proxyrunner)  
   - Include secrets subsystem with fallback logic (pkg/secrets/factory) and authentication flows (pkg/auth/oauth)  
   - Integrate telemetry arrows from API server, CLI, and proxyrunner through middleware to OTLP/Prometheus  

7. Diagram elements to include  
   - Clear labels: “CLI (cmd/thv)”, “Local Runner (cmd/thv-proxyrunner)”, “API Server (pkg/api)”, “K8s Operator (cmd/thv-operator)”, “Container Runtime”  
   - Arrows with annotations: e.g. “HTTP/gRPC”, “Docker API”, “CRD events”, “STDIO/SSE”  
   - Color coding or shape legend:  
     • Client-side tools (blue)  
     • Backend services (green)  
     • Infrastructure/External systems (gray)  
     • Kubernetes components (orange)  

8. Level of detail  
   - Show main Go package layers as boxes only if deeply focusing on code modularity; otherwise, abstract to “Transport”, “Secrets”, “Registry”, “Auth”, “Telemetry.”  
   - Explicitly call out pluggable factories (registry providers, secret stores).  
   - Capture the dual-mode execution: local vs. cluster.  
   - Don’t crowd—use sub-diagrams if needed:  
     • Local execution flow  
     • Kubernetes reconciliation flow  
     • Service mesh (proxyrunner transport)  

By following these guidelines you’ll produce a comprehensive, accurate diagram that reflects ToolHive’s hybrid CLI/API/Operator architecture, its modular Go-based design, and its interactions with external systems. Ensure that every arrow and color corresponds to a well-defined component or flow in the codebase.  
</explanation>
